translation_en: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us; Nafi ibn Umar narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: Asma reported from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: “I will be at my Basin, waiting for whoever comes to me. Some people will be taken away from me, and I will say: ‘They are my community.’ It will be said: ‘You do not know what they did after you; they turned back on their heels.’” Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: “O Allah, we seek refuge in You from turning back on our heels or being put to trial.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Wail, who said: Abdullah said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “I will precede you at the Basin. Men from among you will be brought to me, and when I reach out to give them water, they will be pulled away from me. I will say: ‘Lord, they are my companions.’ He will say: ‘You do not know what they introduced after you.’”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; Yaqoub ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, who said: I heard Sahl ibn Sad say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “I will precede you at the Basin. Whoever reaches it will drink from it, and whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again. Some people will come to me whom I recognize and who recognize me, but then a barrier will be placed between me and them.”

Abu Hazim said: Al-Numan ibn Abi Ayyash heard me relating this and asked: “Did you hear Sahl say that?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “I bear witness that I heard Abu Said al-Khudri add to it: ‘They are from me.’ It will be said: ‘You do not know what they changed after you.’ I will say: ‘Away, away with those who changed things after me.’”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Zayd ibn Wahb narrated to us: I heard Abdullah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to us: “After me you will see others given preference over you and matters that you will disapprove of.” They said: “What do you command us, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Give them their due, and ask Allah for your due.”

Musaddad narrated to us, from Abd al-Warith, from al-Jad, from Abu Raja, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever dislikes something from his ruler should be patient, for whoever separates from the authority by even a handspan and dies in that state dies a death of the pre-Islamic age.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from al-Jad Abu Uthman. Abu Raja al-Ataridi narrated to me, saying: I heard Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever sees something he dislikes from his ruler should be patient with him, for whoever separates from the community by even a handspan and dies does not die except a death of the pre-Islamic age.”

Ismail narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to me, from Amr, from Bukayr, from Busr ibn Said, from Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah, who said: We visited Ubadah ibn al-Samit while he was ill and said: “May Allah restore you to health; tell us a hadith you heard from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, by which Allah may benefit you.” He said: The Prophet called us and we pledged allegiance to him. Among the terms he took from us was that we would listen and obey in times of enthusiasm and reluctance, hardship and ease, and when others are given preference over us; that we would not dispute authority with its rightful holders unless we saw clear disbelief for which we had proof from Allah.

Muhammad ibn Ararah narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Usayd ibn Hudayr: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “Messenger of Allah, you appointed so-and-so but did not appoint me.” He said: “After me you will see others given preference over you, so be patient until you meet me.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Amr ibn Yahya ibn Said ibn Amr ibn Said narrated to us, saying: My grandfather informed me: I was sitting with Abu Hurairah in the Prophet's mosque in Medina, and Marwan was with us. Abu Hurairah said: I heard the truthful and trusted one say: “The destruction of my community will be at the hands of young men from Quraysh.” Marwan said: “May Allah curse them, those young men.” Abu Hurairah said: “If I wished, I could name the sons of so-and-so and the sons of so-and-so.” When my grandfather and I went out to the Banu Marwan after they took power in Syria, and he saw them as young men, he would say to us: “Perhaps these are among them.” We said: “You know best.”

Malik ibn Ismail narrated to us; Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Zaynab bint Umm Salamah, from Umm Habibah, from Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, woke from sleep with his face red, saying: “There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs because of an evil that has drawn near. Today an opening the size of this has been made in the barrier of Gog and Magog.” Sufyan formed a circle of ninety or one hundred with his fingers. It was asked: “Will we be destroyed while righteous people are among us?” He said: “Yes, when wickedness becomes widespread.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri. Mahmud narrated to me; Abd al-Razzaq informed us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, climbed onto one of the high fortresses of Medina and said: “Do you see what I see?” They said: “No.” He said: “I see trials falling among your homes like raindrops.”

Ayyash ibn al-Walid narrated to us; Abd al-Ala informed us; Mamar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Said, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Time will draw closer, good deeds will decrease, miserliness will be cast into people's hearts, trials will appear, and killing will become widespread.” They said: “Messenger of Allah, what is al-harj?” He said: “Killing, killing.” Shuayb, Yunus, al-Layth, and Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri also reported it from al-Zuhri, from Humayd, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet.

Ubaydullah ibn Musa narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Shaqiq, who said: I was with Abdullah and Abu Musa, and they said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Before the Hour there will be days in which ignorance descends, knowledge is taken away, and killing becomes widespread. Al-harj means killing.”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Shaqiq narrated to us, who said: Abdullah and Abu Musa sat and spoke. Abu Musa said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Before the Hour there will be days when knowledge is taken away, ignorance descends, and killing becomes widespread. Al-harj means killing.”

Qutaybah narrated to us; Jarir narrated to us, from al-Amash, from Abu Wail, who said: I was sitting with Abdullah and Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with them both. Abu Musa said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say something similar. Al-harj means killing in the language of Abyssinia.

Muhammad narrated to us; Ghundar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Wasil, from Abu Wail, from Abdullah—and I think he attributed it to the Prophet—who said: “Before the Hour there will be days of killing, when knowledge disappears and ignorance becomes widespread.” Abu Musa said: Al-harj means killing in the language of Abyssinia.

Abu Awanah reported from Asim, from Abu Wail, from al-Ashari, that he said to Abdullah: “Do you know which days the Prophet mentioned as days of killing?” He related something similar. Ibn Masud said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Among the worst people are those whom the Hour overtakes while they are still alive.”

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zubayr ibn Adi, who said: We went to Anas ibn Malik and complained to him about what we were suffering from al-Hajjaj. He said: “Be patient. No time will come upon you except that the time after it will be worse, until you meet your Lord.” I heard this from your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ismail narrated to us; my brother narrated to me, from Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, from Ibn Shihab, from Hind bint al-Harith al-Firasiyyah, that Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Messenger of Allah woke one night frightened, saying: “Glory be to Allah! What treasures have been sent down, and what trials have been sent down! Who will wake the women in their rooms”—meaning his wives—“so that they may pray? Many women clothed in this world will be naked in the Hereafter.”

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Nafi, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us.”

Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever takes up arms against us is not one of us.”

Muhammad narrated to us; Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Mamar, from Hammam, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Let none of you point a weapon at his brother, for he does not know; perhaps Satan will make his hand slip, and he will fall into a pit of the Fire.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us. I said to Amr: “Abu Muhammad, did you hear Jabir ibn Abdullah say that a man passed through the mosque carrying arrows, and the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to him: ‘Hold their tips’?” He said: “Yes.”

Abu al-Numan narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir: A man passed through the mosque carrying arrows with their points exposed. He was ordered to hold their tips so that he would not scratch a Muslim.

Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us; Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Burayd, from Abu Burdah, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “When one of you passes through our mosque or our market carrying arrows, let him hold their tips—or grasp them in his palm—so that none of them harms a Muslim.”

Umar ibn Hafs narrated to us; my father narrated to me; al-Amash narrated to us; Shaqiq narrated to us, who said: Abdullah said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Insulting a Muslim is wickedness, and fighting him is disbelief.”

Hajjaj ibn Minhal narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Waqid informed me, from his father, from Ibn Umar, who heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us; Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us; Ibn Sirin narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from Abu Bakrah—and from another man whom I consider more reliable than Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Bakrah—that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, addressed the people and said: “Do you know what day this is?” They said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “I thought you might call it by another name. Is it not the Day of Sacrifice?” They said: “Indeed, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “What land is this? Is it not the sacred territory?” They said: “Indeed, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Your blood, your property, your honor, and your bodies are sacred to one another, like the sanctity of this day, this month, and this land. Have I conveyed the message?” They said: “Yes.” He said: “O Allah, bear witness. Let those present convey it to those absent, for perhaps the one to whom it is conveyed will understand it better.” Then he said: “Do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks.” When the son of al-Hadrami was burned, when Jariyah ibn Qudamah burned him, they said: “Look toward Abu Bakrah.” They said: “This is Abu Bakrah; he can see you.” Abd al-Rahman said: My mother told me from Abu Bakrah that he said: “If they had entered upon me, I would not have struck even with a cane.”

Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks.”
